title: A Mystery in the Wardrobe!
text: Have you ever tried wearing your favorite shirt from last year, but it felt too tight? Did the shirt shrink in the wash, or did something else happen?

title: Time to Think
text: What do you think really happened? Why do your old shoes and clothes suddenly feel too small for you?

content.title: The Magic of Growing
content.description: Just like a tiny seed slowly grows into a tall tree, your body is growing too! Your bones get longer, and your muscles get stronger.

title: What is this called?
text: This amazing change is called **Growth**. When we are born, we are small babies. Then we become toddlers, then children (like you!), and one day, we will become adults.

content.definition: The process of becoming bigger, taller, and stronger as time passes.

content.question: What happens to our body as we get older?
options: It stays exactly the same size.
It grows taller and gets stronger.

content.title: Photo Detective
content.text: Find a photo of yourself when you were a baby. Look in a mirror now. Can you spot three things that have changed about you?

title: Nature's Rule
text: You are not the only one who grows! Every living thing on Earth grows. A tiny caterpillar becomes a butterfly. A small puppy grows into a big dog. Growing is nature's special magic.

content.title: Master of Growth
content.text: Draw a picture of what you think you will look like when you grow up to be an adult. What will be different?
Encourage students to share what they want to be when they grow up. This helps them connect the physical concept of growth with future goals.

title: Everyone is Different
text: Have you noticed that some of your friends are taller, and some are shorter? Some have curly hair, and some have straight hair. Why don't we all look exactly the same?

title: What's Your Guess?
text: If everyone eats food and drinks water, why do we all grow differently?

content.title: The Unique Snowflake
content.description: Imagine millions of snowflakes falling from the sky. No two snowflakes are exactly the same. Just like snowflakes, every human is made with a unique recipe!

title: Unique You!
text: Each of us is **Unique**. This means there is no one else in the whole world exactly like you. Your fingerprints, your smile, and your thoughts are yours alone.

content.definition: Being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.

content.question: Which of these is true about people?
options: People do not have any differences.

content.title: Fingerprint Magic
content.text: Press your thumb on an ink pad and stamp it on a piece of paper. Now ask your friend to do the same. Look closely with a magnifying glass. Are the lines the same? They are unique!

title: Different but Together
text: Even though we all look different and like different things, we can all be friends. Our differences make the world a colorful and interesting place. Imagine if everyone looked the same and liked the same toys—it would be very boring!

content.text: Sometimes children think being different is a bad thing. Remind them that differences are what make each person special and valuable.

content.title: My Unique Favorites
content.text: Make a list of your 3 favorite toys or games. Ask a friend for their list. Compare them to see how your unique interests make you both special!
